title: MuLM Studio
question: What shape reaches self-attention in this PyTorch transformer?
summary: Follow one attention call from the model code to the corresponding node and inspect the tensor on its input edge.
role: I founded MuLM Studio and lead engineering on the local-first PyTorch workspace.

decision.title: Put the explanation beside the connection
decision.description: In the Checks tab, I put plain-language diagnostics beside traced values and kept the raw trace available. In this example, the call site, node, and input edge give readers a precise place to begin inspecting the model.

caseStudy.limitation: The repository also includes a static mode that loads a precomputed graph. Live updates from new code use the tracing backend. The mismatch widths above are illustrative.
caseStudy.learning: A trace becomes actionable when it identifies the operation and the dimensions together. This edge answers what reached attention in the bundled run. Other inputs and edits require a new trace.
caseStudy.planned: I’m building toward a local-first workspace for inspecting your own PyTorch models.
